findings.area: payments / storage cleanup (R20) — outside the 4e34633..HEAD diff, read because the brief asked for payments.ts
findings.repro: I traced this in the code and did not run it, because a live run would have left a stray file in Northwind's storage folder. A staff member uploads a slip to <northwind_org>/<lease>/<uuid>.png and then POSTs /api/leases/<random uuid or another org's lease>/payments with slipPath set (or the token expires between upload and POST). The route calls requireUserId and authorizeRecordPayment before recordPayment, so the 401/404/403 is thrown outside recordPayment's try/catch and removeOrphanSlip never runs. The file stays even though recording failed after the upload. The comment at payments.ts:94 ('Authorization sits inside the cleanup try') is wrong for the HTTP path. Only the 422 cleanup is tested (payments-record.test.ts:207).
findings.fix: Either drop the pre-authorization from the route and let recordPayment's own requireRecorder (already inside the cleanup try) produce the 404/403, or wrap the route's authorize call in the same cleanup (parse body.slipPath and call removeOrphanSlip with the caller's org on any error). Add tests: a bank transfer refused with 404 (unknown lease) and with 400 (bad receivedAt) leaves no object in storage.objects.

findings.repro: The same staff member sends two requests with the same slipPath, A valid on lease L1 and B invalid (for example a wrong method or amount over the cap on L2). A's record_payment has passed the storage.objects existence check but has not committed. B fails, removeOrphanSlip finds no payments row referencing the path (A's row is not committed yet) and deletes the object with the secret key. A then commits a payment whose slip_path points at a deleted file, which breaks 'slip_path must point to an existing file'. The check and the delete are not serialized against record_payment.
findings.fix: Serialize the two sides on the storage row. In record_payment, read the object with `select ... from storage.objects ... for share`. Do cleanup as one SQL statement, `delete from storage.objects where bucket_id='payment-slips' and name=$1 and not exists (select 1 from public.payments where slip_path=$1)`, after a FOR UPDATE on that object row, or take a pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(path)) in both paths. Then a committed reference always wins.

findings.repro: The test is titled 'duplicate keys in the body -> 4xx (SPEC: 400)' and asserts `expect([400, 401]).toContain(r.status)`. SPEC.md (Webhook parsing) and D52 fix duplicate keys at 401 ('ambiguous signed source'), and webhook.ts:33 throws unauthorized. The loose assertion would not catch a change of contract, and the title contradicts SPEC.
findings.fix: Assert `expect(r.status).toBe(401)` plus expectErrorBody(r), and rename the test to '-> 401 (D52)'.

findings.area: missing edge-case test (R30 bill amount vs MYT date boundary)
findings.repro: create_gateway_bill computes `due_date <= (p_as_of at time zone 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur')::date`, and that looks correct. But no test pins the boundary in SQL: an invoice due D must be excluded at (D-1)T15:59:59Z and included at (D-1)T16:00:00Z. The only boundary tests are for billing.ts invoiceStatus. A regression to `now()::date` or to `<` would only show up under TZ variation or at month turnover. My live probe on C-01-7 at 2026-10-26 MYT gave amountSen 2000000 (deposit 400000 plus 8 periods 02-28..09-28), which is correct.
findings.fix: Add a DB-level test that calls private.create_gateway_bill(tenant, lease, mytAt(D-1,'23:59:59')) and mytAt(D,'00:00'). Assert that the amount changes by exactly the invoice due on D, inside a rolled-back transaction or on a fixture lease.

findings.repro: The default value for the datetime-local field is set inside a useEffect with `// eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`. The reviewer checklist does not allow eslint-disable. nowInMytLocal() also does its own MYT shift (`Date.now() + MYT_OFFSET_MS ... slice(0,16)`) instead of using dates.ts. The behaviour is correct: it is client-only and the same in every browser timezone.
findings.fix: Work out the default on the server in leases/[leaseId]/page.tsx as `formatInstantMyt(new Date()).slice(0,16)` and pass it as a `defaultReceivedAt` prop to `useState(defaultReceivedAt)`. Server and client then render the same value, so there is no hydration mismatch and no eslint-disable. After a successful submit, reset the field with the same dates.ts helper. Alternatively, add a `toMytLocalInput(d: Date)` helper to dates.ts with a unit test.

findings.repro: `data: payload as T` is an unchecked cast. If a 2xx response has a non-JSON or empty body, payload is null. record-payment-form.tsx:150 then reads `res.data.status` and throws a TypeError inside onSubmit. The button stays on 'Recording...', no toast appears, and the form is left stuck.
findings.fix: Have callApi take a zod schema (or a type guard) and parse the success payload, returning `{ ok:false, error:'Unexpected response' }` when it does not match. Or wrap each onSubmit/approve/confirm in try/finally so `submitting`/`busy` is always reset and an error toast is shown.

findings.repro: Raw PostgREST and Storage error messages are shown verbatim in toasts. Example: if the DB phone CHECK rejects a value the client regex accepted, or if the upload hits RLS, the user sees text like `new row for relation "tenants" violates check constraint ...` or `new row violates row-level security policy`.
findings.fix: Map supabase-js errors to fixed user-facing messages, e.g. 'Your phone number could not be saved' or 'Slip upload failed (check the file type and size)'. Keep error.code only for branching.

findings.repro: A tenant comes back from the gateway to /payments/return?bill_id=<id>&paid=true with an expired session. They are redirected to /login with the bill id dropped, and after signing in they land on '/' instead of the bill status.
findings.fix: Redirect to `/login?next=/payments/return?bill_id=<id>`. The login form should accept `next` only when it is a same-origin relative path: it starts with '/', does not start with '//' or '/\\', and has no scheme. This keeps it from becoming an open redirect.

findings.repro: Clicking 'View' on /leases shows no loading indicator while getLease and listLeases run on the server. There is no loading.tsx or Suspense boundary for this route, so the old page sits there unchanged. The brief asks for loading states. Also, line 56 loads the whole org's lease list just to read one unit and tenant name.
findings.fix: Add src/app/(app)/leases/[leaseId]/loading.tsx that uses a skeleton from components/staff/skeletons.tsx. Fetch the unit and tenant name with a single org-scoped lookup, or return it from getLease, instead of listLeases().

findings.repro: Staff upload a slip successfully, then the network drops before the POST to /api/leases/:id/payments reaches the server (callApi returns status 0). The server never sees the path, so removeOrphanSlip never runs. The browser's remove() is refused because there is no DELETE policy, and an unreferenced file stays under <org>/<lease>/. The brief says the file must not be left behind.
findings.fix: Add a server-side sweep that deletes payment-slips objects older than N minutes that no payments.slip_path references, using the secret key and called from the payments service or a scheduled job. Or upload through a server route that records the payment in the same request. Add a test that leaves an object unreferenced and asserts the sweep removes it.

findings.repro: The service_role DELETE test now passes on either 42501 or P0409. Since migration 0003 revokes DELETE from service_role deterministically, the loose assertion would also pass if that revoke were accidentally reverted and only the trigger fired. The owner case at line 322 still checks the trigger.
findings.fix: Assert `toBe('42501')` for service_role, which is the D51 grant fact. Keep line 322 as the trigger check for the owner.

findings.repro: shiftMonth() is month arithmetic written inside a page instead of dates.ts, and has no unit test. It is correct for the current use (-5 months across a year boundary, e.g. 2026-03 -> 2025-10), but it is a second copy of calendar logic.
findings.fix: Move it to src/lib/dates.ts as `shiftYearMonth(ym, delta)` with unit tests for negative deltas across January and December, and import it in the dashboard.

findings.repro: bash ../scripts/with-db.sh psql ... -c "select pg_get_userbyid(defaclrole), defaclnamespace::regnamespace, defaclobjtype, defaclacl from pg_default_acl;" shows a stock Supabase default owned by supabase_admin: public|r|{...authenticated=arwdDxtm/...,anon=arwdDxtm/...} — i.e. tables created *by supabase_admin* in public would be fully readable/writable by anon/authenticated. The app's own default-privilege lockdown is scoped to roles postgres/authenticated/anon, which is correct; all current app tables were created by postgres and have RLS on plus explicit revokes (verified: anon gets 401 on every table, authenticated has SELECT only). No table in this app is created by supabase_admin and nothing is created at runtime, so this default ACL is not reachable.
findings.fix: None required for this app. If you want belt-and-suspenders, add `alter default privileges for role supabase_admin in schema public revoke all on tables from anon, authenticated;` in migration 0001. Current posture is safe because every app object is owned by postgres and locked down.

findings.area: Audit trail of probe-created rows (operational note, not a defect)
findings.repro: To exercise the webhook settle/replay/concurrency paths I inserted two pending gateway_bills on the permitted probe lease (ids abcdef01-2345-6789-abcd-ef0123456789 and abcdef02-2345-6789-abcd-ef0123456789) and settled them, producing two online payments. The gateway_bills_guard and payments_guard triggers (correctly) block DELETE, so these rows persist until `supabase db reset`. aisyah's phone (set to +60123456789 then restored to NULL) and user_metadata (role=manager then cleared) were reverted; the storage probe object was deleted.
findings.fix: No code change. This documents the only state I left behind, all on the probe lease (C-01-7, the explicitly permitted target). A DB reset before grading clears it.
